analysis.title: Unilever Q3 Review: UBSe +1%/+3%/+3%; Momentum meets headwinds
key_insights: Unilever Q3 underlying sales growth (USG) was +5.2% vs company-compiled consensus +4.8%, down from +5.8% in Q2. Underlying volume growth (UVG) was +2.9% vs consensus +2.5%, the third consecutive quarter of volume ahead of the Street this year. Price (UPG) of +2.3% was in line.

The beat came from Emerging Markets (60% of sales, 6.0% volume growth). Asia Pacific Africa USG was +10.1% vs consensus +6.7%, with India +15% (volume +7%) and Indonesia +7%. Developed markets missed.

Shares fell 2% on the day, underperforming the EU Food & HPC sector by 2%. UBS (Sell rating) gives three reasons: weak Foods, a lower 2026 gross margin outlook, and tougher volume comparisons from Q4.

Foods USG was +0.1% vs consensus +1.3%, with UVG at -1.1%, no improvement vs Q2 in sales growth and worse volume. Weak market share momentum plus guidance for higher Foods commodity costs next year point to a difficult 2027 ahead of the McCormick (MKC) deal, after which Unilever shareholders will own 55% of the new MKC.

Management now expects H2 gross margin below H1 (46.8%) because of commodity cost headwinds and negative mix from strong Home Care growth. UBS flags concern that the current under-recovery of input costs is boosting volume share in the short term but weakens the group's earnings growth model if not corrected.

Net material inflation is now about €900m for 2026 (previously €850m or more in UBS's wording, and the top of the previous €800-900m range per the call) and €700m-1bn for 2027. Inflation is lower in HPC and higher in Foods next year. Management says it needs to price at 1.4-1.5x inflation to protect percentage margins.

Volume comparisons get harder from Q4, especially in emerging markets: average UVG was +5.2% in 4Q25-3Q26 vs +0.5% in 4Q24-3Q25. UBS expects UVG to normalise. UBS says this overhang and risk to the 2-3% UVG ambition make a material re-rating unlikely.

FY26 guidance: USG stays at 4-6%, volume raised to at least 3% UVG (from around 3%), H2 USG around 5%, now more balanced between volume and price. Underlying operating margin is guided to a modest improvement vs 20.0% in 2025. FX headwind is now -2% on sales and 30bps on operating margin (previously -3% and 20bps). UBS sees limited change to consensus, since H2 USG 4.8% and UVG 2.2% were already in numbers.

Segment results: Home Care USG +9.1% (consensus +6.7%, UVG +5.4%), Personal Care +6.3% (consensus +5.4%, UVG +3.8%), Beauty & Wellbeing +5.7% (consensus +5.2%), Foods +0.1% (consensus +1.3%). All three HPC categories beat.

Regional weakness: North America USG -0.7% vs consensus +1.4% (UVG -2.5% vs +0.7%), though management says it gained volume share. Europe USG -1.7% vs consensus +0.5%, with price -1.3%. Management expects the US to return to growth in Q4.

Wellbeing declined in Q3 (partly Amazon Prime Day phasing). Nutrafol fell high single digits in Q3 with higher consumer acquisition costs, Olly and LiquidIV declined in Q3. Management sees no structural issue and expects Wellbeing to outperform the market again from H2 2027.

Capital markets day (CMD) in NYC on November 4. UBS expects a new savings programme to offset €400-500m of stranded costs from the Foods separation (the €800m productivity programme finished in June), a reiterated 4-6% USG ambition including 2-3% UVG, and possibly a medium-to-long-term underlying operating margin ambition of 21-23% (vs 19.1% in 2025).

UBS estimate changes: FY26 USG 5.0% with UVG +3.3%, implying Q4 USG 5.0% (price +3.0%, UVG +2.0%), operating margin 20.1% (+10bps y/y), EPS up 1% on FX. FY27 USG 3.5% with UVG 1.0%, margin 20.2% (+10bps), EPS up about 3% on FX.
Valuation: about 17x 2027E P/E, in line with large-cap EU Food & HPC. Another section cites 17.9x P/E 2026 and 17.3x P/E 2027.

market_movers.rationale: UBS Research keeps its Sell on Unilever. It cites weak Foods, gross margin pressure from input costs and mix, and tougher volume comparisons from Q4 that limit re-rating.

Unilever Foods is being combined with McCormick, with Unilever shareholders to own 55% of the new MKC. Foods is weak in developed markets, and antitrust talks may require asset disposals in some markets.

sector_views.rationale: Unilever trades at about 17x 2027E P/E, in line with large-cap EU Food & HPC peers. UBS sees a re-rating of Unilever as unlikely given the Foods overhang and normalising volumes.

earnings_insights: Unilever Q3 2026 (reported 10/29): underlying sales growth +5.2% vs company-compiled consensus +4.8% (UBSe +5.0%), compared with +5.8% in Q2. Volume +2.9% vs consensus +2.5% (UBSe +3.2%). Price +2.3% vs consensus +2.3% (UBSe +1.7%).
Q3 turnover was €13,271m, about 1% above consensus, with a +0.6% FX tailwind and +0.8% net M&A impact.
Q3 USG by division, reported vs value-added (VA) consensus: Home Care +9.1% vs +6.7%, Personal Care +6.3% vs +5.4%, Beauty & Wellbeing +5.7% vs +5.2%, Foods +0.1% vs +1.3%.

Q3 USG by region, reported vs consensus: Asia Pacific Africa +10.1% vs +6.7%, Latin America +8.5% vs +8.4%, North America -0.7% vs +1.4%, Europe -1.7% vs +0.5%. Hindustan Unilever USG was +14.8% (UVG +7%).

FY26 guidance: USG 4-6% unchanged, UVG at least 3% (from around 3%), H2 USG around 5%, modest underlying operating margin improvement vs 20.0% in 2025. Consensus FY26 before the print: USG +4.8% (price +1.6%, volume/mix +3.2%), adjusted EBIT margin 20.1% (+20bps y/y), adjusted EPS €3.23 (+5% y/y).

UBS estimates (not reported figures): FY26 USG 5.0% with UVG +3.3%, Q4 USG 5.0% (price +3.0%, UVG +2.0%), operating margin 20.1%. FY27 USG 3.5%, UVG 1.0%, margin 20.2%. FY26 EPS raised about 1% and FY27 EPS about 3%, both on FX.
Indonesia grew +7% USG led by volume, but gross margin was down 390bps y/y and 190bps q/q.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Input cost pressure is higher than earlier guidance and is pushing H2 gross margin below H1.
Management expects inflation to be lower in HPC and higher in Foods, with El Nino a risk to H2 costs.
Headwind is smaller than the prior guide of -3% on sales and -20bps on margin, which drives UBS's EPS increases.

risk_factors: Foods weakness in developed markets (Germany, Eastern Europe, US condiments) with no quick fix on mayonnaise pricing and pack architecture.
Input cost under-recovery may be unsustainable. It boosts volume share now, but without corrective pricing it weakens the earnings growth model.
Tougher emerging-market volume comparisons from Q4 put the 2-3% UVG ambition at risk.
Foods commodity inflation expected higher in 2027, with vegetable and palm oil exposure and El Nino risk in H2.
McCormick transaction overhang: antitrust may force asset disposals and Unilever shareholders will own 55% of the combined food business.
Wellbeing weakness (Nutrafol acquisition costs, private label in hydration powder) and Europe pricing pressure from buying alliances and promotions.
Brazil tax changes and elections, which management says are covered by guidance.
vol_and_positioning: Shares fell 2% on the day after the print, underperforming the EU Food & HPC sector by 2%, despite a volume-led beat.
geopolitical: Management said global crude output is back to pre-war levels and supply has normalised, but pricing still carries a very high risk premium. Management sees no supply security issues because oil supply has improved.

tension_points.theme: Unilever volume momentum vs cost recovery
tension_points.bull_case: Volume is running ahead of the Street for the third time this year, with 60% of turnover gaining or holding share, FY26 UVG guided to at least 3%, and management pricing at 1.4-1.5x inflation in 2027 to recover costs.
tension_points.bear_case: UBS (Sell) says current input cost under-recovery is boosting volume share in the short term but weakens earnings growth if uncorrected. Tougher emerging-market comparisons from Q4 point to UVG normalisation and Foods stays weak into 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Pricing that fails to cover 2027 inflation (€0.7bn-1bn) or UVG falling below the 2% volume floor management says it will protect.

theme_stances.key_argument: A material re-rating is unlikely given the Foods overhang and risks to the 2-3% UVG ambition over the next 12 months.
theme_stances.evidence: make a material re-rating of the shares unlikely
